plan_a_advantages: Includes tempo runs to improve lactate threshold, a key component of speed.
Features hill workouts to build strength and power for trail ascents and descents.
Offers a greater variety of run types (long, hills, tempo, easy) leading to more well-rounded development.
Higher total training volume (565 minutes vs 489) may be beneficial for continued aerobic development, assuming the athlete is recovering well.
plan_b_advantages: Simpler structure might be easier to adhere to, potentially improving consistency.
Higher proportion of long, easy runs could be beneficial for building base endurance, particularly if the athlete is new to trail running.
reasoning: Plan A appears to be the better choice for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. While both plans incorporate long runs and rest days, Plan A includes a wider variety of workouts – hills, tempo runs, and varying distances of easy runs – which is crucial for developing speed and strength on trails. The inclusion of tempo runs specifically targets lactate threshold, a key factor in improving running speed. Plan B, with its focus primarily on long, easy runs, risks neglecting the development of speed and power needed for efficient trail running.
